questions.q: You arrive ten minutes late to class. What is a polite thing to say?
questions.e: I’m sorry I’m late est une excuse polie.

questions.q: You are on a bus and want to know when it reaches the market. What do you ask?
o: Could you tell me when we reach the market?
Do you know the bus driver?
questions.e: Could you tell me…? sert à demander poliment.

questions.q: At a market, you want to know the price of a bag. What do you ask?
questions.e: How much does this cost? demande le prix.

questions.q: You are lost and need directions to the station. What do you say?
o: Could you show me the way to the station?
questions.e: Show me the way demande le chemin.

questions.q: You forgot a pencil and want to use your friend's pencil. What do you ask?
o: May I lend you a pencil?
questions.e: May I borrow…? demande à emprunter quelque chose.

questions.q: You did not hear the teacher. What do you say?
o: Could you say that again, please?
questions.e: Could you say that again? demande de répéter poliment.

questions.q: You missed a call and want to speak later. What do you say?
questions.e: Call you back veut dire rappeler.

questions.q: Your friend suggests studying together, and you agree. What do you say?
o: That sounds like a good idea.
questions.e: That sounds like a good idea exprime son accord.

questions.q: You cannot attend a party. Which is a polite reply?
o: I'm afraid I can't make it.
questions.e: I’m afraid I can’t make it est une manière polie de refuser.

questions.q: Your friend passed an exam. What do you say?
questions.e: Congratulations félicite quelqu’un pour une réussite.

questions.q: You offer a visitor some tea. What do you ask?
o: Do you like my tea yesterday?
questions.e: Would you like…? sert à offrir quelque chose.

questions.q: You suggest going for a walk. What do you say?
o: We don't go for walk yesterday.
Why don't we go for a walk?
questions.e: Why don’t we…? sert à proposer une activité.

questions.q: Your friend has a headache. What is a kind suggestion?
questions.e: You should donne un conseil.

questions.q: You cannot find your notebook. What do you ask your classmate?
o: Did you see my notebook tomorrow?
questions.e: Have you seen…? sert à demander si quelqu’un a vu un objet.

questions.q: You need permission to leave class early. What do you ask?
questions.e: May I…? sert à demander la permission.

questions.q: The bus is late. What can you tell your friend?
questions.e: Is running late veut dire est en retard.

questions.q: You do not know the meaning of a word. What do you ask?
o: How much does this word cost?
questions.e: What does… mean? demande le sens d’un mot.

questions.q: A classmate helped you carry your books. What do you say?
questions.e: Thanks for your help remercie pour l’aide.

questions.q: You introduce your friend to your teacher. What do you say?
questions.e: This is… sert à présenter quelqu’un.

questions.q: You want your friend's opinion about a film. What do you ask?
o: How do you think the film?
What do you feel the film?
When do you think the film?
What do you think of the film?
questions.e: What do you think of…? demande une opinion.

questions.q: You need your teacher to wait briefly. What do you say?
o: Could you wait a moment, please?
Could you wait an hour yesterday?
questions.e: Could you…? formule une demande polie.

questions.q: You invite a friend to join your group. What do you say?
o: Do you want us to come you?
Would you like to come with us?
questions.e: Would you like to…? sert à inviter poliment.

questions.q: Your little brother is crossing a busy street. What do you say?
questions.e: Be careful! veut dire fais attention.

questions.q: Your cousin has a football match tomorrow. What do you say?
questions.e: Good luck! souhaite bonne chance.
